speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and what specific movements or positions seem to aggravate the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are a 58-year-old male with a 1-year history of burning neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and increasing bilateral hand weakness over the last 3 months, complicated by diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. Given your risk factors and progressive motor symptoms, have you noticed any clumsiness with buttons or difficulty holding objects, and do you have any numbness in the middle finger specifically?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs—specifically fasciculations (UMN) alongside absent reflexes and muscle weakness (LMN)—in the absence of sensory deficits strongly points to this diagnosis.
